title: No Frobenius-fixed compatible class on an open normal curve
statement:
Let $U_0/\mathbf F_q$ be normal, geometrically connected,
separated and of finite type,
pure of dimension one, and put
$U=U_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. If
$\ell\nmid q$, then for the
geometric Frobenius

$$
\left(\varprojlim_nH^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}
(U,\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)\right)^{\Phi_q=1}=0.
\tag{5.4}
$$

The scheme and Frobenius conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-tw-frobenius-action].

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-curve-normal-smooth-compactification] to the given normal, geometrically connected, separated finite-type curve $U_0/\mathbf F_q$. It supplies a smooth projective geometrically connected curve $C_0$, a dense open immersion $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$, and a finite reduced boundary $D_0$. Write $C,U,D,j$ for their geometric base changes, put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ for $n\geq1$, and fix an arbitrary compatible tuple $z=(z_n)_n$ with $\Phi_qz=z$. In particular $\Phi_qz_n=z_n$ for every $n$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: choose the compactification

proof.text: Use [lem-wf-open-curve-residue-sequence] for $(C_0,D_0)$; its coefficient condition holds since $\ell\nmid q$. Compatibility of its residue maps with coefficient reduction shows that $r_n=\operatorname{res}_n(z_n)$ defines an element $r$ of $\varprojlim_nH^0(D,A_n(-1))$. Frobenius equivariance gives $\Phi_qr_n=\operatorname{res}_n(\Phi_qz_n)=r_n$. For the integer $m\geq1$ and $Q=q^m$ supplied by that lemma, iterating this equality gives $\Phi_Qr=r$. The lemma says that the fixed subgroup of this inverse-limit boundary module is zero, so $r=0$, and therefore $r_n=0$ for every $n$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: residues and the positive Frobenius power

proof.text: For every $n$, exactness of (5.1) in [lem-wf-open-curve-residue-sequence], together with $\operatorname{res}_n(z_n)=0$, gives $x_n\in H^1(C,A_n)$ with $j^*x_n=z_n$; the initial zero in (5.1) makes this lift unique. Denote coefficient reduction on either cohomology group by $\rho_n$. The compatibility clause of the same lemma gives $j^*(\rho_nx_{n+1})=\rho_n(j^*x_{n+1})=\rho_nz_{n+1}=z_n=j^*x_n$. Injectivity of $j^*$ implies $\rho_nx_{n+1}=x_n$. Similarly, its Frobenius equivariance gives $j^*(\Phi_qx_n)=\Phi_q(j^*x_n)=\Phi_qz_n=z_n=j^*x_n$, and injectivity implies $\Phi_qx_n=x_n$. Thus $x=(x_n)_n$ is a compatible $\Phi_q$-fixed tuple on $C$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: unique lifts, compatibility, and equivariance

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-proper-curve-compatible-h1-no-fixed] to $C_0/\mathbf F_q$, taking the prime power called $Q$ in that statement to be $q$ here. The curve is smooth, projective and geometrically connected by step 1, and $\ell\nmid q$ is the original hypothesis. Step 3 gives an element of exactly its fixed inverse-limit group, so $x=0$. Consequently $z_n=j^*x_n=0$ for all $n$, whence $z=0$ by coordinatewise equality of compatible tuples. Since $z$ was arbitrary, (5.4) follows.
